subgenres.desc: Dissonant form of polyphonic singing from the regions of Herzegovina and Dalmatia.

subgenres.name: Greek Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Greek folk traditions.

subgenres.name: Aegean Islands Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Music of the Greek Aegean Islands.

subgenres.name: Cretan Folk Music

subgenres.name: Taquirari

subgenres.name: Tonada chilena
subgenres.desc: Traditional folk from the Chilean countryside distinguished by its prominent melody.

subgenres.name: Yaraví
subgenres.desc: Peruvian criollo-mestizo songs with recurring themes of sadness and unrequited love, usually in 6/8 meter.

subgenres.name: Zamacueca
subgenres.desc: Traditional genre and dance of 19th century Peru, sung in the minor mode and accompanied by a varying combination of guitar, vihuela, harp and cajón.

subgenres.name: Zamba
subgenres.desc: Folk dance that evolved out of Peruvian Zamacueca during the 19th century.

subgenres.name: Indigenous American Traditional Music
subgenres.desc: Meta-genre encompassing traditions attributed to the indigenous peoples of the Americas.

subgenres.name: Athabaskan Fiddling
subgenres.desc: Fiddle playing of the Northern Athabaskan Dene people of modern-day Alaska, the Yukon, and the Northwest Territories.

subgenres.name: Ghost Dance Song
subgenres.desc: Songs accompanying the Ghost Dance, a 19th century religious movement.

subgenres.name: Inuit Vocal Games
subgenres.desc: Practiced by the Inuit of Canada, two vocalists face each other decimeters away and try to outlast each other with intense and unusual vocal techniques.

subgenres.name: James Bay Fiddling
subgenres.desc: Fiddle playing of the James Bay Cree people, characterised by a fusion of Scottish style with Cree rhythms.

subgenres.name: Mapuche Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Mapuche people of Chile and Argentina.

subgenres.name: Powwow Music
subgenres.desc: Drum-based traditional music of Plains region Native American tribes, traditionally played at Pow-wows.

subgenres.name: Rabbit Song
subgenres.desc: Indigenous North American ceremonial song cycles most associated with Southern Paiute, Ute, Mojave, and Chemehuevi traditions which feature short, repetitive, vocable-heavy melodies performed in long sequences that accompany trickster (rabbit) narratives and encode social knowledge.

subgenres.name: Tonada potosina
subgenres.desc: Traditional folk sung in Quechua, played on charangos and guitarillas, with a catchy, lively rhythm.

subgenres.name: Unakesa
subgenres.desc: Lay song and dance of the Fulni-ô people.

subgenres.name: Indigenous Australian Traditional Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of Aboriginal Australians and Torres Strait Islanders, collectively known as Indigenous Australians.

subgenres.name: Djanba
subgenres.desc: Sung and composed in the Murrinh-Patha language and consisting of a mixed group of men and women accompanied by bilma and handclaps, typically without didgeridoo.

subgenres.name: Wangga
subgenres.desc: Originated from the Daly region, consists of performances featuring wood sticks, didgeridoo and voice.

subgenres.name: Industrial Folk Song
subgenres.desc: Details the experiences and aspirations of industrial laborers and their working conditions; frequently rooted in labor causes and often used for protest and organizational purposes.

subgenres.name: Ladino Folksong
subgenres.desc: Ladino-language Traditional Folk Music tunes that were written and preserved by Sephardic Jews.

subgenres.name: Ob-Ugric Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Ob-Ugric people of West Siberia Plain.

subgenres.name: Payada
subgenres.desc: Improvised poetry accompanied by a guitar that is tied to gaucho culture, usually performed in duo as a verse duel.

subgenres.name: Romani Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Folk of the Romani people, an ethnic group with origins in Northern India, but who have since the Middle Ages settled around Europe, principally Romania, Bulgaria, and Spain, and many other places.

subgenres.name: Samoyedic Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Samoyedic peoples.

subgenres.name: South Asian Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Meta-genre which covers all the Traditional Folk Music forms from South Asia.

subgenres.name: Assamese Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Assamese people, a people group mostly from the Northeastern Indian state of Assam.

subgenres.name: Bengali Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditions of the Bengali people found mainly in the Indian state of West Bengal and the country of Bangladesh.

subgenres.name: Baul gaan
subgenres.desc: Songs performed by the Bauls, a movement of mystic entertainers influenced by diverse spiritual traditions.

subgenres.name: Bhojpuri Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditions of the Bhojpuri people of India, originally from the states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

subgenres.name: Biraha
subgenres.desc: Call-and-response style of folk music developed from the Ahir and neighboring castes of the Bhojpuri people.

subgenres.name: Boduberu
subgenres.desc: Traditional, percussion-based form of music popular in the Maldives, usually following a crescendo structure.

subgenres.name: Burushaski Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Burusho people of northern Pakistan.

subgenres.name: Gujarati Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Gujarati people, who primarily live in the western Indian state of Gujarat.

subgenres.name: Kannada Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Kannada people, a large ethnolinguistic group who mainly inhabit the state of Karnataka in southwestern India.

subgenres.name: Kirtan
subgenres.desc: Call-and-response chanting that involves the singing of devotional mantras and hymns in a bhakti devotional style, occasionally accompanied with traditional folk instrumentation.

subgenres.name: Shabad kirtan
subgenres.desc: Religious Sikh Hymn backed by specially selected ragas and taal.

subgenres.name: Malayali Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of Kerala, India primarily sung in the Malayalam language and known for its drumming and percussion.

subgenres.name: Mappila
subgenres.desc: Traditional folk music from Kerala's Malabar region, sung in Arabic inflected Malayalam (Arabi Malayalam), blending Islamic devotional themes with local poetic forms.

subgenres.name: Marathi Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Marathi people, a large ethnic group who mainly inhabit the state of Maharashtra in western India.

subgenres.name: Newa Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditions of the Newa people, who live in Nepal, performed with mostly percussive instruments and some wind instruments.

subgenres.name: Odia Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Odia, a large ethnic group who mainly inhabit the state of Odisha in eastern India.

subgenres.name: Pashto Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Pashtun people of southern Afghanistan and north-western Pakistan.

subgenres.name: Punjabi Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Punjabi people, mostly from the Punjab regions of India and Pakistan, covering diverse styles often played with traditional instruments.

subgenres.name: Rajasthani Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditions of the Rajasthani people of Western India - who now mostly live in the eponymous Rajasthan state - originated across the various castes that inhabit the region.

subgenres.name: Sinhalese Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Folk of the Sinhalese people, the majority ethnic group of Sri Lanka.

subgenres.name: Sarala gee
subgenres.desc: Blend of Hindustani Classical Music with Sinhalese Folk Music.

subgenres.name: Tamil Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Tamil people.

subgenres.name: Urumi melam
subgenres.desc: Percussive ensemble native to the Tamil Nadu region, taking its name from the urumi drum.

subgenres.name: Telugu Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Telugu people, one of the largest ethnolinguistic groups of India, mainly living in the states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

subgenres.name: Burrakatha
subgenres.desc: Traditional form of narrative music, featuring a tambura player paired with two drummers who interrupt the main storyteller to provide additional remarks.

subgenres.name: Southeast Asian Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Meta-genre covering all folk forms from Southeast Asia, like Gondang, Hmong, Iban, Karen, Keroncong, Khmer, Lao, Lun Bawang, Molam, and Orang Ulu.

subgenres.name: Balitaw
subgenres.desc: Folk originating in the Visayas islands of the Philippines; dialogue or debate in which a man and a woman compete at improvising romantic verses.

subgenres.name: Bamar Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the majority ethnic group of Myanmar.

subgenres.name: Gondang
subgenres.desc: Traditional ensemble in Bataknese traditional music of North Sumatra, taking its name from its leading instrument - a unique set of toned drums.

subgenres.name: Harana
subgenres.desc: Hispanic-influenced lyrical courtship music traditionally sung by men, accompanied by guitar based on the danza rhythm.

subgenres.name: Hmong Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Folk traditions of the Hmong people, an ethnic group localized in Laos, Vietnam, China, and Thailand.

subgenres.name: Khmer Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Folk of the Khmer people, who mainly reside in Cambodia.

subgenres.name: Kuda kepang
subgenres.desc: Accompanies a traditional Javanese dance of the same name, featuring a stripped-back version of a Gamelan ensemble that removes softer instruments.

subgenres.name: Lao Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Lao people.

subgenres.name: Malay Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Malay people, who are native to Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, northern Indonesia, and southern Thailand.

subgenres.name: Philippine Rondalla
subgenres.desc: Ensemble of plucked string instruments typically performed for traditional Filipino folk dances; known for its distinct sparkling and tinkling tremolo sound.

subgenres.name: Tarawangsa
subgenres.desc: Sacred ceremonial music originating in the Rancakalong district, played with the jentreng harp and the tarawangsa bowed lute.

subgenres.name: Thai Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Thai people.

subgenres.name: Fon leb
subgenres.desc: Traditional performance music originating in northern Thailand consist of an ensemble with Piphat instruments and a pair of female choreographers.

subgenres.name: Vietnamese Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Vietnamese people, with traditions influenced by both Chinese Music and Austronesian culture through the Cham people.

subgenres.name: Chèo
subgenres.desc: Northern Vietnamese folk musical theatre, characterized by minimal set design and satirical content.

subgenres.name: Quan họ
subgenres.desc: Tradition of the Northern Vietnamese provinces of Bắc Ninh and Bắc Giang, originally consisting of harmonic, a cappella singing from two competing duos.

subgenres.name: Xẩm
subgenres.desc: Developed in Northern Vietnam, traditionally sung by blind bards accompanied by a đàn bầu or đàn nhị.

subgenres.name: West Asian Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of West Asia, a region that covers much of what is commonly known in English as the Middle East (alternatively Southwestern Asia), includes the distinct but interconnected traditions of numerous ethnic groups.

subgenres.name: Alevi Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Anatolian folk pioneered by Turkish poets and bards, connected to the Alevist heterodox Islamic tradition.

subgenres.name: Armenian Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Armenians, which is attested in historic Armenia since antiquity, with unique regional dialects unified by general melodic structure.

subgenres.name: Kef Music
subgenres.desc: Dance-oriented Armenian American music with prominent presence of Anatolian instruments and folkloric melodies (often in the 10/8 meter) paired with novel lyrics relating to a variety of topics.

subgenres.name: Assyrian Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Folk of the Assyrian or Syriac people, who are indigenous to the Upper Mesopotamian region roughly corresponding to ancient Assyria (which includes modern-day northern Iraq, northwestern Iran, northeastern Syria, and southeastern Turkey).

subgenres.name: Ayyalah
subgenres.desc: Traditional Khaliji-Bedouin weapon performance, commonly found across the United Arab Emirates and Northwestern Oman.

subgenres.name: Fijiri
subgenres.desc: Deeply rooted in the Persian Gulf pearl diving culture, and sung during weekly gatherings combining solo and choral sections with minimal percussion.

subgenres.name: Israeli Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Folk of the Jewish settlers of Eretz Yisra'el.

subgenres.name: Luri Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Luri people of southwestern Iran.

subgenres.name: Meyxana
subgenres.desc: Azerbaijani folk recitative genre.

subgenres.name: Persian Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of the Persian people.

subgenres.name: Turkish Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Traditional Folk Music of Turkish people combines the distinct cultural heritages and traditions of Anatolian civilisations and former Ottoman territories.

subgenres.name: Turkish Black Sea Region Folk Music
subgenres.desc: Folk of the Turkish people who inhabit the northern region by the Black Sea.

subgenres.name: Uzun Hava
subgenres.desc: Semi-improvisational melodic structure in Turkish Folk Music.

subgenres.name: Zeybek
subgenres.desc: Turkish Folk Music music and dance that originated with the Zeybek people during the Ottoman Empire period, with slow and asymmetrical rhythms.

subgenres.name: Work Song
subgenres.desc: Sung by laborers and prisoners while working in factories and fields.

subgenres.name: Aboio
subgenres.desc: Cattle-herding songs originating in rural Northeastern Brazil.

subgenres.name: Aboio cantado
subgenres.desc: Aboio that features rhyming verses.

subgenres.name: Field Hollers
subgenres.desc: Created by African-American slaves working on cotton plantations, featuring expressive vocals to no strict rhythm.

subgenres.name: Haozi
subgenres.desc: Chinese Work Song that originated from collective manual labor and usually follows a call-and-response structure, aiming to coordinate work.

subgenres.name: Military Cadence
subgenres.desc: Call-and-response work song performed by military personnel.

subgenres.name: Òrain luaidh
subgenres.desc: Rhythmic call-and-response style song form that traditionally accompanied the production of tweed cloth through beating the material by hand to soften it after it came off the loom.

subgenres.name: Sea Shanty
subgenres.desc: Songs originally sung by sailors to coordinate work on ships.

subgenres.name: Shan'ge
subgenres.desc: Folk songs found in upland regions of China, typically sung while working.

subgenres.name: Yodeling
subgenres.desc: Vocal technique that arose in many cultures around the world as a form of calling and communication.

subgenres.name: Country Yodeling
subgenres.desc: Vocal technique of Yodeling, brought to the United States by German settlers, sung over the instrumentation of Traditional Country.

subgenres.name: Naturjodel
subgenres.desc: Originated in Toggenburg and Appenzell in Switzerland; deep vocal range, relaxed voice, free tempo, polyphony, elongated notes, improvisation, glissando, and use of syllabic sounds.

name: Hip Hop
desc: Emerged primarily on the United States East Coast in African-American communities in the late 1970s; emphasizes rhythmic beat patterns and a type of spoken vocal delivery known as rapping.

subgenres.name: Abstract Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Uses much more abstract lyricism than what is considered conventional within the genre, typically through use of metaphors, symbolism, and cryptic meanings.

subgenres.name: Afroswing
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the United Kingdom during the mid-2010s, incorporating influences from Dancehall, Afrobeats, Contemporary R&B, and a variety of West African Music.

subgenres.name: Afro Trap
subgenres.desc: Centered mostly in France, features production influenced by modern styles developed in West and Central Africa with Trap-styled vocal flows.

subgenres.name: Arabesque Rap
subgenres.desc: Emerged from Turkey in the late 2000s, based almost exclusively around Arabesk samples and featuring aggressive rap vocals.

subgenres.name: Bongo Flava
subgenres.desc: Tanzanian genre originating in the mid-1990s in the Dar es Salaam area, combining the influence of Rhythm & Blues, Afrobeat, and Dancehall with native Tanzanian styles like Taarab and Muziki wa dansi.

subgenres.name: Boom Bap
subgenres.desc: Production style identified by an acoustic-sounding drum pattern of a kick drum on the downbeat followed by a cracking snare on the upbeat.

subgenres.name: Bounce
subgenres.desc: Developed in New Orleans in the early 1990s; initially defined by a slow to midtempo beat with a double-time hi-hat pattern on top and syncopated “twerk” rhythms of eighth-note claps.

subgenres.name: Sissy Bounce
subgenres.desc: Energetic style associated with New Orleans’ LGBT culture, featuring punchy drums, hyper-repetitive vocal chops, and sexually explicit chants.

subgenres.name: Chipmunk Soul
subgenres.desc: Sped-up vocal samples and slick, soulful production.

subgenres.name: Chopped and Screwed
subgenres.desc: Remixing technique that consists of skipping effects ("chopping") and dropping the tempo ("screwing").

subgenres.name: Christian Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Employs lyrics with a pro-Christianity message to profess the performer's faith, often to attract attention from new potential converts.

subgenres.name: Cloud Rap
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the early 2010s, known for its relaxed, dream-like, and reverb-heavy production style, taking influence from Chillwave, and producers' obscure sample choices.

subgenres.name: Comedy Rap
subgenres.desc: Primarily intended to be humorous, through the use of comedic lyrics, production, delivery, or other musical aspects.

subgenres.name: Chap Hop
subgenres.desc: Satirises British cultural stereotypes with posh rapping and a distinctive retro aesthetic drawn from the "chap" and steampunk subcultures, often with elements of Music Hall.

subgenres.name: Conscious Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Features lyrics about social issues.

subgenres.name: Country Rap
subgenres.desc: Combines the flow, production-emphasis, and demeanor of Hip Hop with the lyrical content and general approach of Country.

subgenres.name: Crunk
subgenres.desc: Synthesis of various Southern US club music scenes into an raucous, drum machine-based sound featuring synthesizer stabs, call-and-response chants, and uptempo drumming derived from Memphis Rap.

subgenres.name: Crunkcore
subgenres.desc: Combines rapping, screaming and autotune with synthesizers and Hip Hop beats often influenced by Crunk.

subgenres.name: Detroit Sound
subgenres.desc: Upbeat 808 percussion; simple, funky mallet instruments, keys, strings, and synth bass; and street-centric, often punched-in rapping.

subgenres.name: Flint Sound
subgenres.desc: Uptempo and repetitive, featuring simple melodies, pitched-up snares, and humorous, punchline-heavy lyrics.

subgenres.name: Philly Drill
subgenres.desc: Apocalyptic and haunting choirs, keys, and strings with gruesome narratives and slow, sparse drums.

subgenres.name: Digicore
subgenres.desc: Developed in the late 2010s and characterized by frantic, bombastic, and glamourous production, usually derived from Trap, that serves to accompany highly melodious, auto-tuned, and hi-pitched vocal performances, often done with breathy voice singing and sing-rapping.

subgenres.name: Dirty South
subgenres.desc: Originated in the Southern US during the mid-1990s, defined by a bouncy rhythm, fast-tempo snares, 808s, heavy bass, and often rapped in a rhythmic delivery consisting of explicit lyrics.

subgenres.name: Disco Rap
subgenres.desc: Most prevalent from 1979 to 1982, featuring MCs rapping over popular Disco breaks.

subgenres.name: Drill
subgenres.desc: Originated in Chicago in the early 2010s; broadly characterized by complex, energetic rhythms coupled with gang-oriented, street-conscious, and violent lyrics.

subgenres.name: Chicago Drill
subgenres.desc: Bass-heavy, dense, and typically syncopated percussion, featuring ticking hi-hats and gunshot-like snare rolls, usually accompanied by menacing synth melodies and violent Gangsta Rap lyricism.

subgenres.name: Bop
subgenres.desc: Grew out of the Chicago Drill scene in the early 2010s, characterized by autotuned vocals and upbeat synth melodies.

subgenres.name: Free Car Music
subgenres.desc: Chaotic and metallic percussion with clanging rides, rapid hi hat rolls, and tense kick buildups typically coupled with staggered, punched-in rapping.

subgenres.name: Jersey Drill
subgenres.desc: Mixes Drill and Jersey Club production, characterized by an energetic sound and distinct syncopated rhythms.

subgenres.name: New York Drill
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the late 2010s, characterized by energetic, bouncy tresillo rhythms, creating a warmer, more booming tone than UK Drill, which prominently inspired it.

subgenres.name: Sample Drill
subgenres.desc: Prominent, recognizable samples set to tresillo-styled Drill hi-hats and counter snares.

subgenres.name: Sexy Drill
subgenres.desc: Emotive and sensual melodies, samples, and basslines set to driving stomps and bouncy Drill percussion typically joined by lyrical themes of sex, love, clubbing, and heartbreak.

subgenres.name: Philly Drill
subgenres.desc: Apocalyptic and haunting choirs, keys, and strings with gruesome narratives and slow, sparse drums.

subgenres.name: UK Drill
subgenres.desc: Deep bass and complex rhythm which denotes a Grime influence in the production.

subgenres.name: Drumless
subgenres.desc: Stripped-down production style pioneered in the early 2010s and identified by a lack of drums or minimal, subtle percussion left untouched from the original sample or filtered out.

subgenres.name: Emo Rap
subgenres.desc: Moody, melancholic production combining atmospheric Cloud Rap, and Trap's typical drum programming, with sampling from Alternative Rock, Midwest Emo, Emo-Pop, and Pop Punk.

subgenres.name: Experimental Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Incorporates experimental and eccentric elements considered unconventional or unorthodox compared to more traditional hip hop.

subgenres.name: Industrial Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Incorporates harsh elements inspired by Industrial music such as blaring, noisy synths, distorted and metallic percussion, as well as more aggressive and off-kilter rapping styles.

subgenres.name: Genge
subgenres.desc: Combines elements of Dancehall with various traditions of Kenya.

subgenres.name: Gengetone
subgenres.desc: Takes strong influence from Reggaetón and modern Dancehall, featuring more explicit lyrics and harder beats.

subgenres.name: G-Funk
subgenres.desc: Relaxed and organic sound featuring live instrumentation, use of P-Funk samples, and high-pitched synth lines.

subgenres.name: Hardcore Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Confrontation and aggression, whether in the lyricism, vocal delivery, hard beats, heavy production, or any combination thereof.

subgenres.name: Britcore
subgenres.desc: British subgenre from the late 1980s and early 1990s featuring fast breakbeats and rapping.

subgenres.name: Chopper
subgenres.desc: Originated in the Midwest Hip Hop scene in the 1990s; initially defined by slow jam beats rapped over with very fast flows and resonant choruses.

subgenres.name: Gangsta Rap
subgenres.desc: Lyrics from a gangster's perspective.

subgenres.name: Coke Rap
subgenres.desc: Lyrics with heavy reference to street-level drug dealing, specifically cocaine.

subgenres.name: Mafioso Rap
subgenres.desc: Themed around organized crime, particularly the Mafia, often featuring cinematic production and lavish aesthetics.

subgenres.name: Road Rap
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the mid 2000s from Brixton and Peckham featuring abrasive tones, prominent Grime influence, and lyrics depicting circumstances of street gang violence in the UK.

subgenres.name: Scam Rap
subgenres.desc: Lyrics that focus on various forms of fraudulent activities.

subgenres.name: Horrorcore
subgenres.desc: Lyrical and aesthetic focus on the macabre and morbid, with production generally of a darker nature than is typically found in other Hip Hop.

subgenres.name: Memphis Rap
subgenres.desc: Minimalistic half-time drum machine programming with droning bass, often paired with aggressive rapping and a double time flow.

subgenres.name: Dungeon Rap
subgenres.desc: Combines the dark production of Memphis Rap with the fantasy aesthetics and sound design of Dungeon Synth.

subgenres.name: Phonk
subgenres.desc: Modernized, eclectic take on classic Memphis Rap production, featuring various influences from other Hip Hop genres, especially drum programming inspired by other Southern Hip Hop as well as frequent jazzy, funky elements somewhat akin to West Coast Hip Hop and from Electronic music.

subgenres.name: Mid-School Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Based around heavy, stripped-down drum machine beats.

subgenres.name: Trap Metal
subgenres.desc: Loud, distorted 808s and basslines, as well as aggressive vocals that are usually yelled or screamed.

subgenres.name: Hipco
subgenres.desc: Developed in Liberia, often featuring conscious and political lyrics and influences from local dance styles.

subgenres.name: Hiplife
subgenres.desc: Fusion of Ghanaian Highlife with Hip Hop.

subgenres.name: Houston Sound
subgenres.desc: Features slow to medium tempos, heavy bass, prominent organs and horns, and live instruments such as keyboards, bass guitar and wah-wah pedal.

subgenres.name: Hyphy
subgenres.desc: Party-focused style with upbeat tempos, heavy bass and prominent synths, all underpinned by a distinctive West Coast-style rhythm, claps on beats 2 and 4, and a strong kick drum on beats 1, 2, and either 3 or 4.

subgenres.name: Jerk Rap
subgenres.desc: Sparse beats, simple melodies, and party-centric lyrics geared towards a style of dance called “jerkin’.”

subgenres.name: Instrumental Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Can take the form of instrumental versions of songs that normally feature rapping, or hip hop originally released and always intended to be instrumental.

subgenres.name: Rare Phonk
subgenres.desc: Primarily features eclectic sampling and lush, jazzy beats, usually set to Trap rhythms with prominent influences of Memphis Rap.

subgenres.name: Jazz Rap
subgenres.desc: Incorporates elements of Jazz through the use of samples or live instrumentation.

subgenres.name: Jerk
subgenres.desc: Sparse, snare-heavy drum patterns loosely inspired by Jerk Rap, which take major elements from other prominent 2010s and 2020s underground hip hop genres like Plugg.

subgenres.name: Jersey Club Rap
subgenres.desc: Incorporates Jersey Club's distinct kick-heavy rhythms, which are modified to better suit rapping, featuring less sampling and more atmospheric production than earlier Jersey club.

subgenres.name: Jersey Drill
subgenres.desc: Mixes Drill and Jersey Club production, characterized by an energetic sound and distinct syncopated rhythms.

subgenres.name: Jigg
subgenres.desc: Club-oriented genre characterized by heavy 808-driven beats, imposing synthesized brasses and an uptempo rhythm.

subgenres.name: Jook
subgenres.desc: Eclectic mix of influences on booty bass music developed in Tampa and Miami in the mid-2000s revolving around uptempo rhythms, airy chords, and party-oriented lyrics.

subgenres.name: Latin Rap
subgenres.desc: Primarily done in Spanish; incorporates Hispanic American Music elements into its sound.

subgenres.name: Chicano Rap
subgenres.desc: Latin Rap with a Mexican twist.

subgenres.name: Lo-Fi Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Relaxed, laid-back form of Hip Hop, typically instrumental and influenced by Jazz Rap and Downtempo.

subgenres.name: Lowend
subgenres.desc: Rhythms driven by steady eighth-note digital handclaps, rattling bass, fast tempos, upbeat sound, and laid-back flows.

subgenres.name: Miami Bass
subgenres.desc: Sustained Roland TR-808 kick drums and faster tempos, along with a distinct Electro influence.

subgenres.name: Atlanta Bass
subgenres.desc: Originated in Atlanta, slower tempos and a more melodic approach than Miami Bass.

subgenres.name: Tamborzão
subgenres.desc: Adds Afro-Brazilian percussive elements such as the atabaque sound into the Miami Bass kick drums.

subgenres.name: Techno Bass
subgenres.desc: Minimal, stripped-down with an emphasis on low-frequency bass partitions.

subgenres.name: Car Audio Bass
subgenres.desc: Slow and minimalistic extreme form, focused on ultra-low frequency sine wave notes and mainly intended for stress testing subwoofer sound systems.

subgenres.name: Mobb Music
subgenres.desc: San Francisco Bay Area production style that samples slowed down Funk to create a slow, pounding, and menacing sound with live studio instrumentation and Roland TB-303 basslines.

subgenres.name: Motswako
subgenres.desc: Mainly rapped in a mixture of Setswana and English, incorporating additional languages and local South African and Botswanan influences, particularly Kwaito.

subgenres.name: Nerdcore Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Themes touch on such nerd mainstays as science, computers, and science fiction.

subgenres.name: Nervous Music
subgenres.desc: Dark, sinister and menacing sound, heavy sub-basses, simple melodies and slow, sparse and slamming drums.

subgenres.name: Philly Club Rap
subgenres.desc: Mixes the fast and energetic production of Philly Club with similarly frantic and fast rapping.

subgenres.name: Political Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Features explicitly political lyrics and themes.

subgenres.name: Pop Rap
subgenres.desc: Fuses Hip Hop's rapping and production traits with Pop elements such as melodious vocals and light, catchy tunes.

subgenres.name: Bop
subgenres.desc: Grew out of the Chicago Drill scene in the early 2010s, characterized by autotuned vocals and upbeat synth melodies.

subgenres.name: Frat Rap
subgenres.desc: Light-hearted and laid-back with lyrical focuses on subjects such as partying and college life.

subgenres.name: Futuristic Swag
subgenres.desc: Playful tone with bright square wave melodies, singsong rapping, joyful intonations, and triumphant brass leads.

subgenres.name: Ratchet
subgenres.desc: Club-oriented style defined by a repeated synth melody and a sparse drum pattern often accompanied by a "hey" chant.

subgenres.name: Sigilkore
subgenres.desc: Dark and hyperactive production, featuring rapping laced with layers of effects.

subgenres.name: Snap
subgenres.desc: Sparse production, pounding 808 bass, occasional use of third-beat finger snaps, and simple melodies reminiscent of ringtones.

subgenres.name: Stoner Rap
subgenres.desc: Heavily features lyrics about cannabis and stoner culture, usually with a laid-back flow and relaxing production.

subgenres.name: Trap
subgenres.desc: Originated in Atlanta in the early 2000s; distinctive fast hi-hat sound and heavy bass at moderate tempos.

subgenres.name: Chicago Drill
subgenres.desc: Bass-heavy, dense, and typically syncopated percussion, featuring ticking hi-hats and gunshot-like snare rolls, usually accompanied by menacing synth melodies and violent Gangsta Rap lyricism.

subgenres.name: Bop
subgenres.desc: Grew out of the Chicago Drill scene in the early 2010s, characterized by autotuned vocals and upbeat synth melodies.

subgenres.name: Free Car Music
subgenres.desc: Chaotic and metallic percussion with clanging rides, rapid hi hat rolls, and tense kick buildups typically coupled with staggered, punched-in rapping.

subgenres.name: Futuristic Swag
subgenres.desc: Playful tone with bright square wave melodies, singsong rapping, joyful intonations, and triumphant brass leads.

subgenres.name: New Jazz
subgenres.desc: Colorful, repetitive synths and synthetic instruments, playful vocal chops, and wonky bass selections set to bouncy Trap drums.

subgenres.name: No Melody
subgenres.desc: Usage of minimalistic, repetitive midtempo drum patterns, and simple, prominent 808s.

subgenres.name: Plugg
subgenres.desc: Use of sparse and compact drum and hi-hat patterns, subby 808s and heavy low end; commonly features piano samples, airy pads, and icy synths.

subgenres.name: Ambient Plugg
subgenres.desc: Strong atmosphere and texture taken from Ambient music; featuring tight drums and minimal low-end and 808s.

subgenres.name: Dark Plugg
subgenres.desc: Ominous, sinister synth pads and lead melodies, skittering hi-hats, and fast percussion and snare rolls.

subgenres.name: PluggnB
subgenres.desc: Emphasizes more melodic and layered synth leads, denser and faster drum programming, and a lesser reliance on the laid-back, minimalistic atmosphere of earlier Plugg styles.

subgenres.name: Asian Rock
subgenres.desc: Dense PluggnB percussion in combination with airy bells, synth plucks, and soaring synthetic guitar leads.

subgenres.name: Terror Plugg
subgenres.desc: Harsher and noisier, with 808s distorted to create a high-frequency sound.

subgenres.name: Rage
subgenres.desc: Dense, buzzing synth work with repetitive chord progressions and melodic synth leads.

subgenres.name: Rare Phonk
subgenres.desc: Primarily features eclectic sampling and lush, jazzy beats, usually set to Trap rhythms with prominent influences of Memphis Rap.

subgenres.name: Regalia
subgenres.desc: Lush, sweeping string arrangements, dreamy piano passages, and other orchestral instrumentation set to cinematic Trap percussion.

subgenres.name: Trap latino
subgenres.desc: Distinguished by its Reggaetón and Latin Rap roots, with smooth and moody production inspired by Alternative R&B and Contemporary R&B.

subgenres.name: Trap Metal
subgenres.desc: Loud, distorted 808s and basslines, as well as aggressive vocals that are usually yelled or screamed.

subgenres.name: Trap Soul
subgenres.desc: Mixes passionate vocals derived from Contemporary R&B with laid-back, nocturnal and atmospheric Trap production.

subgenres.name: Tread
subgenres.desc: Icy or futuristic synths with busy and high-tempo drum programming using distinctive 808 patterns.

subgenres.name: Trap shaabi
subgenres.desc: Combining Trap percussion and rhythms with Egyptian Shaabi and especially Mahraganat.

subgenres.name: Turntablism
subgenres.desc: Manipulating and re-appropriating vinyl records using a turntable and DJ mixer in a Hip Hop context, often featuring constant scratching and beat juggling between two or more recordings into original, distinctive tracks.

name: Industrial & Noise
desc: Umbrella encompassing Noise and Industrial, as well as later derivatives that combine the latter aesthetics with other styles and in more accessible directions which fall under Post-Industrial.

subgenres.name: Industrial
subgenres.desc: Emerged out of Punk and avant-garde art movements in the mid-1970s, often characterized by a bleak, mechanical atmosphere, the use of metallic percussion as well as other unconventional instruments, and extensive use of sampling influenced by Musique concrète.

subgenres.name: Power Electronics
subgenres.desc: Waves of feedback, screeching analog synthesizers, and harsh, screamed vocals.

subgenres.name: Death Industrial
subgenres.desc: Combines the abrasive textures of Noise and Industrial music with dark, brooding drones and atmospheres.

subgenres.name: Noise
subgenres.desc: Strays away from conventional structure, tonality, and composition and consists predominantly of noise.

subgenres.name: Ambient Noise Wall
subgenres.desc: Soft, sparse textures inspired by the static composition of Harsh Noise Wall.

subgenres.name: Black Noise
subgenres.desc: Incorporates unconventional sounds with overpowering or constant Noise and Black Metal elements, often being heavily texture-oriented, abrasive, dissonant, atonal, or repetitive.

subgenres.name: Gorenoise
subgenres.desc: Combines and subverts Goregrind and Grindcore with brash Noise and even faster drum tempos.

subgenres.name: Harsh Noise
subgenres.desc: Highly aggressive walls of sound that assault the listener.

subgenres.name: Harsh Noise Wall
subgenres.desc: Harsh, distorted walls of sound that feature few dynamic variations and often take the form of long compositions with little to no change or progression over time.

subgenres.name: Power Electronics
subgenres.desc: Waves of feedback, screeching analog synthesizers, and harsh, screamed vocals.

subgenres.name: Death Industrial
subgenres.desc: Combines the abrasive textures of Noise and Industrial music with dark, brooding drones and atmospheres.

subgenres.name: Power Noise
subgenres.desc: Combines looped samples of Noise with Electronic rhythms.

subgenres.name: Post-Industrial
subgenres.desc: Umbrella group of genres that combine the dark, mechanical aesthetic of early Industrial music with more accessible genres, such as Rock and Electronic Dance Music.

subgenres.name: Dark Ambient
subgenres.desc: Emphasizes an ominous, gloomy, and dissonant atmosphere.

subgenres.name: Black Ambient
subgenres.desc: Incorporates elements such as guitars, synthesizers, harsh or whispered vocals, raw production, or other elements associated with Black Metal and Dungeon Synth.

subgenres.name: Ritual Ambient
subgenres.desc: Dark, disturbing, ritualistic, and occult atmosphere, often taking inspiration from various existing ritual practices around the world.

subgenres.name: Deconstructed Club
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the 2010s as the hybridization of diverse Electronic Dance Music genres with an abrasive Post-Industrial sound.

subgenres.name: EBM
subgenres.desc: Melodic and dancefloor-friendly take on Post-Industrial music that developed in the early 1980s.

subgenres.name: Dark Electro
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the early 1990s in Europe, incorporating the abrasiveness of old school Industrial but with a greater focus on a horror-inspired atmosphere and harsh, distorted vocals.

subgenres.name: Aggrotech
subgenres.desc: Merges aggressive-sounding synths and apocalyptic atmospheres with harsh 4/4 beats and fast tempos.

subgenres.name: Futurepop
subgenres.desc: Derivative of EBM, retaining its apocalyptic worldview but incorporating heavy influence from the melodic style of Synthpop.

subgenres.name: New Beat
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the mid-1980s in Belgium; characterized by dark basslines, hard-hitting grooves and a slow tempo.

subgenres.name: Hard Beat
subgenres.desc: Short-lived, harder, harsh form of New Beat with Industrial, Acid House and EBM-influenced arrangement.

subgenres.name: Electro-Industrial
subgenres.desc: Formed in the late 1980s and early 1990s; grew out of a combination of EBM and Industrial.

subgenres.name: Dark Electro
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the early 1990s in Europe, incorporating the abrasiveness of old school Industrial but with a greater focus on a horror-inspired atmosphere and harsh, distorted vocals.

subgenres.name: Aggrotech
subgenres.desc: Merges aggressive-sounding synths and apocalyptic atmospheres with harsh 4/4 beats and fast tempos.

subgenres.name: Industrial Hardcore
subgenres.desc: Fuses the sonic palettes and aesthetics of Industrial with the intense rhythms of Gabber, Speedcore, Doomcore and other subsequent styles.

subgenres.name: Industrial Hip Hop
subgenres.desc: Incorporates harsh elements inspired by Industrial music such as blaring, noisy synths, distorted and metallic percussion, as well as more aggressive and off-kilter rapping styles.

subgenres.name: Industrial Metal
subgenres.desc: Incorporates the abrasive and heavy sound of Industrial into Metal, using elements like synthesizers and drum machines.

subgenres.name: Cyber Metal
subgenres.desc: Originated around 1999, influenced by EBM and Aggrotech with more melodic and less repetitive riffs as well as harsh vocals.

subgenres.name: Neue Deutsche Härte
subgenres.desc: Alternative Metal and Industrial Metal that incorporates various aspects of electronic music, specifically Electronic Dance Music.

subgenres.name: Industrial Rock
subgenres.desc: Incorporates abrasive guitars and synthesizers inspired by Industrial and various Post-Industrial styles.

subgenres.name: Machine Rock
subgenres.desc: Emphasises a mechanical sound that centres heavy, Punk Rock-inspired guitar riffs over Electro-Industrial beats, while incorporating cyberpunk themes and imagery.

subgenres.name: Industrial Techno
subgenres.desc: Harder, darker style of Techno which draws parallels with factories and the rhythm of machinery.

subgenres.name: Birmingham Sound
subgenres.desc: Cold, mechanical, and hypnotic tracks, typically lacking the harsher and noisier elements of later Industrial Techno.

subgenres.name: Martial Industrial
subgenres.desc: Incorporates elements of traditional European military marches with Neoclassical Darkwave, Dark Ambient, Industrial, and Neofolk.

subgenres.name: Power Noise
subgenres.desc: Combines looped samples of Noise with Electronic rhythms.

name: Jazz
desc: Originating in African American communities in the Southern United States around the turn of the 20th century, building on New Orleans Brass Band ensemble and influences from Ragtime and Blues to become a very popular style by the emergence of Swing in the 1930s.

subgenres.name: Afro-Jazz
subgenres.desc: African-styled percussion and rhythms.

subgenres.name: Arabic Jazz
subgenres.desc: Blending of Arabic Music and Jazz.

subgenres.name: Avant-Garde Jazz
subgenres.desc: Combines traditional or mainstream Jazz stylings with non-traditional techniques of avant-garde art music by experimenting with characteristics such as rhythm, harmony, structure, melody, and instrumentation.

subgenres.name: Experimental Big Band
subgenres.desc: Dispensing with traditional Jazz structures and Swing sounds, instead performing Avant-Garde Jazz and pushing the boundaries of the medium.

subgenres.name: Free Jazz
subgenres.desc: Attempts to break free from the conventions and patterns of earlier Jazz subgenres through the use of elements such as dissonance, atonality, and free-flowing rhythmic structures.

subgenres.name: European Free Jazz
subgenres.desc: Arose in Europe in the late 1960s and early 1970s, moving even further from the Jazz tradition by often dropping the swinging rhythm, taking liberties with the use of atonality and noise.

subgenres.name: Bebop
subgenres.desc: Fast tempos, improvisation, melodic chromaticism, and complex harmonies and chord progressions.

subgenres.name: Big Band
subgenres.desc: Commonly associated with the golden era of Swing in the 1930s and 1940s, performed by a large ensemble including brass, woodwinds, and usually a rhythm section.

subgenres.name: Experimental Big Band
subgenres.desc: Dispensing with traditional Jazz structures and Swing sounds, instead performing Avant-Garde Jazz and pushing the boundaries of the medium.

subgenres.name: Progressive Big Band
subgenres.desc: Introduces Western Classical Music compositional techniques into Big Band.

subgenres.name: British Dance Band
subgenres.desc: Came from the dancehalls of the 1920s and 1930s, combining a British take on Jazz with the Music Hall tradition.

subgenres.name: Bulawayo Jazz
subgenres.desc: Emerged from the city of Bulawayo, Zimbabwe in the early 1950s, led by the alto sax and accompanied by ensembles.

subgenres.name: Cape Jazz
subgenres.desc: Developed parallel to American Jazz in the early 20th century, named for its origin in Cape Town, South Africa.

subgenres.name: Cartoon Music
subgenres.desc: Zany and uptempo; incorporates elements of Western Classical Music and Modern Classical into frantic Big Band arrangements, playfully chaotic to match the on-screen actions of Cartoon characters and the beat of their movements.

subgenres.name: Chamber Jazz
subgenres.desc: Made by mostly small acoustic-based ensembles with emphasized improvisation and influenced by Neoclassicism and Traditional Folk Music.

subgenres.name: Cool Jazz
subgenres.desc: Developed in the late 1940s alongside and in response to Bebop, featuring a more restrained, emotionally "cool" style.

subgenres.name: Crime Jazz
subgenres.desc: Gritty, moody style that emerged in the mid-1950s to accompany film noir movies and hard-boiled detective/crime-themed TV shows.

subgenres.name: Dark Jazz
subgenres.desc: Melancholic and gloomy Film noir-inspired atmosphere and influence from Crime Jazz and Dark Ambient.

subgenres.name: Dixieland
subgenres.desc: Developed in New Orleans in the 1910s, incorporating influences from Ragtime and Blues into cacophonous, polyphonic arrangements with instruments trading places between accompaniment and soloist.

subgenres.name: ECM Style Jazz
subgenres.desc: Primarily associated with ECM Records, combining elements of Jazz Fusion with the subdued atmosphere of Cool Jazz and the Western Classical Music bent of Third Stream.

subgenres.name: Ethio-Jazz
subgenres.desc: Unique blend of traditional Ethiopic Music and Jazz.

subgenres.name: Flamenco Jazz
subgenres.desc: Combination of Jazz with Flamenco nuevo, the contemporary style of Flamenco, which was pioneered in the late 1960s.

subgenres.name: Hard Bop
subgenres.desc: Continuation of Bebop that reintroduces more traditional African-American musical features, such as bluesy melodies, slow to medium tempos, and a more groove-oriented sound, while retaining the expressive improvisation.

subgenres.name: Indo Jazz
subgenres.desc: Fuses the various musical traditions of the Indian subcontinent with jazzy musical structures.

subgenres.name: Jazz-Funk
subgenres.desc: Jazz highly influenced by Funk.

subgenres.name: Jazz Fusion
subgenres.desc: Near-universal usage of electric guitars and keyboards coupled with influences from genres such as Rock, Rhythm & Blues, Funk, and Traditional Folk Music, and a relative degree of harmonic simplicity.

subgenres.name: Jazz manouche
subgenres.desc: Combines Jazz with several aspects of Romani Folk Music.

subgenres.name: Jazz Poetry
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the 1920s, incorporating the style and rhythms of Jazz as both art forms spread throughout African-American communities in the United States.

subgenres.name: Kréyol djaz
subgenres.desc: Combines Jazz with various styles of French Caribbean Music.

subgenres.name: Latin Jazz
subgenres.desc: Fusion with Latin American rhythms, especially those of African origin.

subgenres.name: Afro-Cuban Jazz
subgenres.desc: Combines Jazz with the rhythms of Afro-Cuban music.

subgenres.name: Samba-jazz
subgenres.desc: Jazz genre from Brazil that incorporates Samba and/or Bossa nova elements.

subgenres.name: Marabi
subgenres.desc: South African Jazz with origins in the 1920s and rooted in traditional South African music.

subgenres.name: Kwela
subgenres.desc: Influenced by Zulu music, characterized by its happy melodies, played by pennywhistle flutes and accompanied by a banjo or a guitar.

subgenres.name: Mbaqanga
subgenres.desc: Emerged from the traditional Marabi Jazz and Swing as well as Kwela popular South African genres.

subgenres.name: Modal Jazz
subgenres.desc: Utilizes musical modes as harmonic framework over traditionally used chord progressions.

subgenres.name: Jazz Mugham
subgenres.desc: Combines Jazz with elements of Azerbaijani Mugham, featuring jazz-inspired instrumental compositions, improvisations, wind and vocal elements, as well as modal scales and ornamentation techniques for emotional depth.

subgenres.name: Post-Bop
subgenres.desc: Grew out of Hard Bop in the early to mid-1960s incorporating certain untraditional elements inspired largely in part from Avant-Garde Jazz, Modal Jazz and eventually, Free Jazz, such as non-diatonic chord progressions, irregular rhythms and amelodic forms.

subgenres.name: Smooth Jazz
subgenres.desc: Simple melodies and slick production influenced by Pop and R&B.

subgenres.name: Soul Jazz
subgenres.desc: Appeared during the 1950s when Gospel, Rhythm & Blues and later Soul started to influence the style of prolific Jazz musicians.

subgenres.name: Spiritual Jazz
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the 1960s, marked by a mixture of Jazz with approximations of ethnic styles, religious music of non-Christian traditions, and the ecstatic, transcendental aspects of Free Jazz.

subgenres.name: Spy Music
subgenres.desc: Meant to evoke the action and drama of Spy films.

subgenres.name: Stride
subgenres.desc: Early form of Ragtime-derived Jazz with improvisational tendencies; named for the performers' left hand "striding" across the piano keyboard.

subgenres.name: Sweet Jazz
subgenres.desc: Early form developed by white bandleaders and highly popular with white audiences in the 1920s, emphasizing arrangements and strong melodies with a straighter rhythmic feel, de-emphasizing improvisation compared to "hot" Dixieland.

subgenres.name: Swing
subgenres.desc: Distinctive rhythm and large backing rhythm section over which solos are performed.

subgenres.name: Swing Revival
subgenres.desc: Born out of 1990s alternative music; sometimes incorporating elements from newer genres such as Rockabilly, Ska, and Punk Rock.

subgenres.name: Third Stream
subgenres.desc: A fusion of Jazz and Western Classical Music, with improvisation as a vital component.

subgenres.name: Vocal Jazz
subgenres.desc: Focused on vocals, generally using a more traditional, poppy strong structure and reducing the role of improvisation.

subgenres.name: Vocalese
subgenres.desc: Newly written lyrics set to the melody of an existing instrumental solo, often in a Bebop or Big Band style, and characterized by syllabic phrasing.

subgenres.name: West Coast Jazz
subgenres.desc: Laidback style of jazz related aesthetically to Cool Jazz, developed by musicians based in Los Angeles and San Francisco, California in the 1950s.

name: Metal
desc: Driving and distorted riffs, aggressive drumming, vigorous vocals, and an all-around show of brute force in its early days, since branching into dozens of subgenres.

subgenres.name: Alternative Metal
subgenres.desc: Mid-tempo style emphasizing melodicism and rhythmic heaviness; branches outside of the stylistic conventions of Metal.

subgenres.name: Funk Metal
subgenres.desc: Melds Funk Rock grooves with slap basslines and metallic guitarwork.

subgenres.name: Neue Deutsche Härte
subgenres.desc: Alternative Metal and Industrial Metal that incorporates various aspects of electronic music, specifically Electronic Dance Music.

subgenres.name: Nu Metal
subgenres.desc: Emphasizes bouncy, drop-tuned riffs, alternating vocal styles, and genre-bending, often incorporating Hip Hop and Funk Metal elements.

subgenres.name: Rap Metal
subgenres.desc: Features rapped vocals, typically formed around heavy, mid-tempo, and groove-oriented playing in addition to elements of Hip Hop beats such as record scratching.

subgenres.name: Avant-Garde Metal
subgenres.desc: Often breaking the bounds of the genre through experimental structures and instrumentation, or by incorporating outside influences.

subgenres.name: Black Metal
subgenres.desc: Highly distorted, treble-heavy guitars, tremolo-picked riffs, blast beats and double bass drumming, shrieked vocals, and raw, lo-fi production; often focuses on occult, dark imagery and atmosphere.

subgenres.name: Atmospheric Black Metal
subgenres.desc: Repetitive riffs and melodies, slower tempos, synthesized ambient textures, and guitar effects creating atmospheric soundscapes.

subgenres.name: Blackgaze
subgenres.desc: Fuses tremolo-picked riffing, intense drumming and harsh vocal techniques with mellow, dreamy textures, major-key melodies and extended build-ups.

subgenres.name: Black 'n' Roll
subgenres.desc: Incorporates elements of Hard Rock, Glam Rock, and Heavy Metal.

subgenres.name: Black Noise
subgenres.desc: Incorporates unconventional sounds with overpowering or constant Noise and Black Metal elements, often being heavily texture-oriented, abrasive, dissonant, atonal, or repetitive.

subgenres.name: Dissonant Black Metal
subgenres.desc: Dissonant atonal riffing, cleaner production style, and complex song structures.

subgenres.name: DSBM
subgenres.desc: Lethargic, melancholic, and repetitive sound; depressive and misanthropic themes; vocals ranging from high-pitched wails and screams to strained cleans; often featuring non-distorted sections.

subgenres.name: Hellenic Black Metal
subgenres.desc: Black metal scene in Greece with more mid-tempo songwriting and pronounced Heavy Metal influence.

subgenres.name: Melodic Black Metal
subgenres.desc: Stronger emphasis on melody, generally with cleaner production and more diverse arrangements.

subgenres.name: Pagan Black Metal
subgenres.desc: Folk song-inspired melodies, traditional instruments, acoustic guitar passages, and often cleanly sung vocals, centered on romanticized pagan themes and imagery.

subgenres.name: Symphonic Black Metal
subgenres.desc: Symphonic soundscapes, typically but not always synthesized.

subgenres.name: War Metal
subgenres.desc: Aggressive, chaotic, and heavily Death Metal-influenced, featuring muddy, bass-heavy production and often incorporating war-themed lyrics.

subgenres.name: Death Metal
subgenres.desc: Heavily distorted, down-tuned guitars, palm-muted, tremolo-picked riffs, double-kick and blast beat percussion, chromatic chord progressions, minor keys, abrupt changes in tempo, and guttural vocals.

subgenres.name: Brutal Death Metal
subgenres.desc: Emphasizes abrasiveness, chunky rhythmic atonal riffs, and low guttural vocals.

subgenres.name: Slam Death Metal
subgenres.desc: Focuses on slow or midtempo (as well as breakdown-style) sections built on chromatic, palm-muted riffs - so-called "slams".

subgenres.name: Death 'n' Roll
subgenres.desc: Incorporates a groove-oriented, Hard Rock-influenced approach while retaining heavily distorted rhythm guitars and gruff or occasionally growled vocals.

subgenres.name: Deathgrind
subgenres.desc: Combines the intensity and high-pitched screams of Grindcore with the technicality and low guttural vocals of Death Metal.

subgenres.name: Melodic Death Metal
subgenres.desc: Utilizes the guitar harmonies and melodic focus of Heavy Metal while generally retaining down-tuned, heavily distorted guitars and a harsh, aggressive sound.

subgenres.name: Gothenburg Sound
subgenres.desc: Pioneering Melodic Death Metal style and scene of Gothenburg, Sweden.

subgenres.name: Technical Death Metal
subgenres.desc: Focuses on challenging, demanding songwriting and instrumental skill.

subgenres.name: Dissonant Death Metal
subgenres.desc: Emphasizes discordant, dense songwriting and utilizes pinch harmonics, scratchy guitar leads, and atonality.

subgenres.name: Djent
subgenres.desc: Groovy polymeters, syncopated power chord chugs, palm-muted, distorted guitars, and significant focus on production and tone.

subgenres.name: Thall
subgenres.desc: Utilizes rapid release bends and a precise playstyle while contrasting pitch-shifted high and low notes, with ambient sections for atmosphere and buildup.

subgenres.name: Doom Metal
subgenres.desc: Plodding tempos, repeated chords, and thick, distorted, down-tuned guitars in a style focused on foreboding, atmosphere, and tension.

subgenres.name: Death Doom Metal
subgenres.desc: Fuses down-tuned guitars, growled vocals, and aggressive, often double-kick drumming with a mournful, somber atmosphere and plodding tempos.

subgenres.name: Funeral Doom Metal
subgenres.desc: Features exceptionally slow, funeral dirge-like tempos; crushing, sluggish guitars; mournful, melancholic atmosphere; and distant, hushed growls and grunts.

subgenres.name: Traditional Doom Metal
subgenres.desc: Monotonous and heavy playing style; repetitive, rough, and sometimes atonal guitar riffs; a "rocking to sleep" bass; and influences from both Blues Rock and Psychedelic Rock.

subgenres.name: Epic Doom Metal
subgenres.desc: Emphasizes Heavy Metal influence and theatrical vocals.

subgenres.name: Drone Metal
subgenres.desc: Extremely slow tempos, highly sustained, repetitive guitar notes, and minimalist song structures often omitting a traditional rhythm section and vocals.

subgenres.name: Folk Metal
subgenres.desc: Features influences from various types of Traditional Folk Music expressed through melodies and/or traditional instrumentation, notably having a large scene in Europe.

subgenres.name: Celtic Metal
subgenres.desc: Features Celtic Folk Music elements.

subgenres.name: Mittelalter-Metal
subgenres.desc: Emerged as a metallic style in the mid-to-late 1990s from the German Neo-Medieval movement.

subgenres.name: Gothic Metal
subgenres.desc: Usually low-to-mid-tempo songwriting featuring down-tuned, plodding riffing, a somber atmosphere shaped by ample usage of keyboards and synthesizers, and vocal styles ranging from harsh growls to baritone singing and female operatic vocals.

subgenres.name: Grindcore
subgenres.desc: Brief and intense song structures featuring a plethora of blast beats, down-tuned and tremolo-picked guitars, and abrasive, usually raw production.

subgenres.name: Cybergrind
subgenres.desc: Standard conventions of Grindcore taken to an even more discordant and rapid-fire extreme, with added Electronic dimensions of computer-generated noises and drum machines.

subgenres.name: Deathgrind
subgenres.desc: Combines the intensity and high-pitched screams of Grindcore with the technicality and low guttural vocals of Death Metal.

subgenres.name: Goregrind
subgenres.desc: Death Metal-influenced riffs with rhythms ranging from very fast to slower mid-tempos correlated with pitch-shifted vocals, sloppy playing and production, and gore-themed aesthetics.

subgenres.name: Gorenoise
subgenres.desc: Combines and subverts Goregrind and Grindcore with brash Noise and even faster drum tempos.

subgenres.name: Pornogrind
subgenres.desc: Groovy, mid-tempo style known for its exaggerated bouncy rhythm and common pornographic themes.

subgenres.name: Mincecore
subgenres.desc: Raw and simplistic with heavy reliance on Punk structures while including political and socially aware themes.

subgenres.name: Noisegrind
subgenres.desc: Noise-driven, defined by its rawness, feedback usage, and very brief song structures.

subgenres.name: Groove Metal
subgenres.desc: Midtempo riffs influenced by Thrash Metal but with a greater focus on rhythmic syncopation and heaviness over speed.

subgenres.name: Heavy Metal
subgenres.desc: Heavier outgrowth of Hard Rock featuring greater distortion and intensity along with lesser Blues influences.

subgenres.name: Speed Metal
subgenres.desc: Fast tempos, double-time feel, aggressive riffs, precise, often virtuosic soloing and expressive vocal styles.

subgenres.name: US Power Metal
subgenres.desc: American style influenced by NWOBHM that features heavily distorted guitars paired with more aggressive riffs, mid-tempo Heavy Metal rhythms, and over-the-top theatrical vocals with fantasy or conceptual themes.

subgenres.name: Industrial Metal
subgenres.desc: Incorporates the abrasive and heavy sound of Industrial into Metal, using elements like synthesizers and drum machines.

subgenres.name: Cyber Metal
subgenres.desc: Originated around 1999, influenced by EBM and Aggrotech with more melodic and less repetitive riffs as well as harsh vocals.

subgenres.name: Neue Deutsche Härte
subgenres.desc: Alternative Metal and Industrial Metal that incorporates various aspects of electronic music, specifically Electronic Dance Music.

subgenres.name: Kawaii Metal
subgenres.desc: Fuses various Metal substyles with J-Pop's upbeat melodicism and song structures, utilizing kawaii lyricism and an idol music aesthetic.

subgenres.name: Metalcore
subgenres.desc: Drop-tuned guitar riffs, constant double kick drumming with varying tempos and techniques, breakdown sections, and screaming or shouting vocals.

subgenres.name: Deathcore
subgenres.desc: Integrates brutal palm-muted and tremolo-picked riffing, blast beat-focused drumming, and guttural vocals of Death Metal with groovy breakdown sections.

subgenres.name: Downtempo Deathcore
subgenres.desc: Slow and minimal songs emphasizing breakdowns, atmosphere, and dissonance with downtuned guitars.

subgenres.name: Mathcore
subgenres.desc: Rhythmically complex, featuring unconventional time signatures, syncopated and dissonant riffs and erratic metric shifts.

subgenres.name: Melodic Metalcore
subgenres.desc: Originated in the late 1990s when some metalcore bands infused elements of Melodic Death Metal into their sound to create a more metallic and melodic style.

subgenres.name: Thall
subgenres.desc: Utilizes rapid release bends and a precise playstyle while contrasting pitch-shifted high and low notes, with ambient sections for atmosphere and buildup.

subgenres.name: Neoclassical Metal
subgenres.desc: Greatly influenced by Western Classical Music in its style of playing and composing.

subgenres.name: Post-Metal
subgenres.desc: Atmospheric and dense metallic riffs, unconventional songwriting, sonic experimentation, and adoption of eclectic influences.

subgenres.name: Atmospheric Sludge Metal
subgenres.desc: Combines slow, churning guitar riffs and thunderous percussion with dark, extensive otherworldly sonic landscapes.

subgenres.name: Blackgaze
subgenres.desc: Fuses tremolo-picked riffing, intense drumming and harsh vocal techniques with mellow, dreamy textures, major-key melodies and extended build-ups.

subgenres.name: Doomgaze
subgenres.desc: Gloomy and sombre atmosphere, amplified by the slow tempo and melancholy of Doom Metal, combined with the effects, washes of sound, and vocals found within Shoegaze.

subgenres.name: Power Metal
subgenres.desc: Developed from Heavy Metal and Speed Metal, emphasizing speed, vocal melody and harmonized lead guitars.

subgenres.name: Progressive Metal
subgenres.desc: Fuses amplified, guitar-driven sound with technical proficiency, virtuosity, complex compositions, innovative arrangements, eclecticism, and additional instrumentation.

subgenres.name: Sludge Metal
subgenres.desc: Mixes Doom Metal's slow pacing, down-tuned riffing style and dark atmosphere with Hardcore Punk's aggression, abrasiveness and harsh vocals.

subgenres.name: Atmospheric Sludge Metal
subgenres.desc: Combines slow, churning guitar riffs and thunderous percussion with dark, extensive otherworldly sonic landscapes.

subgenres.name: Southern Metal
subgenres.desc: Blues-influenced style that primarily incorporates Sludge Metal and Stoner Metal with metallic Southern Rock riffs.

subgenres.name: Stenchcore
subgenres.desc: Heavier, more metallic form of Crust Punk drawing influence from Thrash Metal as well as Death Metal and Heavy Metal.

subgenres.name: Stoner Metal
subgenres.desc: Combines elements of Doom Metal with elements of Psychedelic Rock and Blues Rock to create a melodic yet heavy sound.

subgenres.name: Symphonic Metal
subgenres.desc: Incorporates elements of symphonic and Orchestral Music.

subgenres.name: Thrash Metal
subgenres.desc: Blistering tempos, palm-muted, technical riffing influenced by Speed Metal, aggressive drumming utilizing double-kick and skank beats, and diverse vocal styles ranging from harsh to clean techniques.

subgenres.name: Crossover Thrash
subgenres.desc: Mixes the metallic instrumentation of Thrash Metal with the ethos and approach of Hardcore Punk.

subgenres.name: Technical Thrash Metal
subgenres.desc: Places great emphasis on complex songwriting and demanding instrumental parts.

subgenres.name: Trance Metal
subgenres.desc: Tempo between 130 and 160 BPM, played with keyboards and metal instrumentation, sung with harsh and aggressive vocals including many clean melodic styles; regularly uses elements of Melodic Death Metal, Symphonic Metal, and Electronic Dance Music.

subgenres.name: Viking Metal
subgenres.desc: Developed out of Black Metal and embodies an epic, Viking-like aesthetic.

name: Musical Theatre and Entertainment
desc: Range of styles of theatre individually popular in the United States or in various countries in Europe, mostly from the 19th century to the mid-20th century.

subgenres.name: Ballad Opera
subgenres.desc: English reaction to the Italian Opera styles with a satirical sense of humor and scores borrowing from Traditional Folk Music and popular music.

subgenres.name: Cabaret
subgenres.desc: Entertainment featuring Comedy, song, dance, and theatre.

subgenres.name: Comédie-ballet
subgenres.desc: French form of musical drama from the 17th century that combines operatic singing, classical dance, and theater.

subgenres.name: Cuplé
subgenres.desc: Originally developed in the 19th century as a blend of old theatre Spanish styles based in short monologues (jácara and tonadilla) and French Couplet.

subgenres.name: Dutch Cabaret
subgenres.desc: Popular comedy form in the Netherlands which evolved out of traditional Cabaret in the 1890s.

subgenres.name: Kabarett
subgenres.desc: Theatrical entertainment consisting of mixed elements of music, sketches, monologues, dialogues, lyric poetry and/or ballads.

subgenres.name: Kanto
subgenres.desc: Songs performed at the Tuluat Theaters of İstanbul in the late 19th century.

subgenres.name: Minstrelsy
subgenres.desc: Popular song and entertainment tradition from the U.S. engendered in variety shows employing racist caricature and blackface.

subgenres.name: Murga
subgenres.desc: Popular carnival music traditional in some cities of Spain and Hispanic America.

subgenres.name: Murga uruguaya
subgenres.desc: Variant originated in Montevideo that stands out for its rhythms, nasal vocals and choral arrangements.

subgenres.name: Music Hall
subgenres.desc: British theatrical entertainment popular in the 19th and 20th centuries, featuring light and comedic popular songs.

subgenres.name: Operetta
subgenres.desc: Light opera interspersed with spoken dialogues, being usually satirical and/or humorous in nature and centered around romantic plots and dancing scenes.

subgenres.name: Kalon'ny fahiny
subgenres.desc: Fusion of music from the highlands of Madagascar and western Operetta.

subgenres.name: Revue
subgenres.desc: French Musical Theatre and Entertainment based on numbers and sketches inspired by the most relevant events of the year.

subgenres.name: Rock Musical
subgenres.desc: Style of musical theatre inspired by Rock.

subgenres.name: Show Tunes
subgenres.desc: Originally composed to forward the story or enhance the characters or other plot elements of Broadway productions and other stage music.

subgenres.name: Siffleur
subgenres.desc: Professional whistlers on the Vaudeville and Music Hall circuits.

subgenres.name: Singspiel
subgenres.desc: German form of Opera distinguished by the prominent usage of spoken dialogues mixed with lyrical or folklore arias/ballads.

subgenres.name: Vaudeville
subgenres.desc: Performed in American musical theaters typically as part of a lowbrow, often comedic variety performance.

subgenres.name: Vaudeville Blues
subgenres.desc: Vaudeville incorporating heavy Blues elements.

name: New Age
desc: Broad genre centered on peaceful, meditative melodies, using a wide variety of instrumentation.

subgenres.name: Andean New Age
subgenres.desc: Takes heavy influence from Indigenous Andean Music, emphasizing a peaceful and harmonious atmosphere and often using the flute.

subgenres.name: Celtic New Age
subgenres.desc: Incorporates influences and performing styles from Celtic Folk Music, emphasizing pastoral imagery and wistful themes.

subgenres.name: Native American New Age
subgenres.desc: Takes heavy influence from Indigenous North American Music, emphasizing a peaceful and harmonious atmosphere and utilizing chants, drumming, and flutes.

subgenres.name: Neoclassical New Age
subgenres.desc: Strongly influenced by and sometimes also based upon early music and the Baroque Music or Classical Period.

subgenres.name: New Age Kirtan
subgenres.desc: American development of Kirtan, fusing it with New Age and Western music.

subgenres.name: Tibetan New Age
subgenres.desc: Incorporates perceived elements of Tibetan Music, particularly singing bowls.

name: Pop
desc: Umbrella of popular styles closely tied to mass production and mass marketing, focusing on catchiness and accessibility through melody, rhythm, lyrics, and hooks.

subgenres.name: Adult Contemporary
subgenres.desc: Slow to midtempo with a light and soothing tone, emerged as a successful radio format in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

subgenres.name: Afrobeats
subgenres.desc: Originated in West Africa during the early 2010s and includes elements from Pop Rap, Contemporary R&B, and Dancehall.

subgenres.name: Afropiano
subgenres.desc: Blends the easy-going, poppy, and melodic Afrobeats sound and rhythms with major Amapiano elements, like lush, jazzy, and laid-back atmospheres often featuring light piano chords.

subgenres.name: Alté
subgenres.desc: More subdued, atmospheric, minimalist, and eclectic production and vocal styles compared to earlier styles, as well as more socially conscious lyrics.

subgenres.name: Alt-Pop
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the late 2000s and early 2010s, combining chart Pop conventions with alternative/indie sensibilities and sometimes more minimal and contemplative atmosphere, often extracted from Alternative R&B.

subgenres.name: Arabic Pop
subgenres.desc: Synthesis of Arabic Music with Western Pop melodies, almost always sung in Arabic and typically performed with Arabic instruments, alongside some Western instruments like the guitar.

subgenres.name: Al jeel
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the 1970s as an alternative to Shaabi, taking influence from foreign Pop and incorporating rhythms of Reggae while retaining a distinctly Egyptian sound.

subgenres.name: Mūsīqā lubnāniyya
subgenres.desc: Lebanese pop genre that emerged post-independence as a nationalist tradition distinct from Egyptian and Levantine music, blending local influences with western orchestration, peaking in Lebanon's 1957–1975 golden age through radio, cinema, and stage.

subgenres.name: Art Pop
subgenres.desc: Inventive, idiosyncratic, or artistically ambitious, often experimenting with unconventional musical elements and conceptual approaches while retaining accessibility.

subgenres.name: Balkan Pop-Folk
subgenres.desc: Balkan popular music which blends Pop, Folk, and ethnic music.

subgenres.name: Chalga
subgenres.desc: Bulgarian blend of Contemporary Folk (Turkish, Bulgarian, Arabic & Romani) with Dance-Pop.

subgenres.name: Manele
subgenres.desc: Mixture of Romanian Music with Turkish, Middle Eastern, Balkan, and Romani influences, usually electronic in production.

subgenres.name: Modern Laika
subgenres.desc: Laiki music mixed with popular Western music, most notably pop and dance.

subgenres.name: Musika popullore
subgenres.desc: Tradition in Albania consisting of light, commercial, amplified Albanian Folk Music usually professionally arranged and manufactured in recording studios alongside video clips.

subgenres.name: Muzică de mahala
subgenres.desc: Appeared in the 1980s, incorporating modern instruments and based on the model of Balkan Pop-Folk in neighboring countries.

subgenres.name: Skiladika
subgenres.desc: Greek popular artists who used more Arabian elements; originally a derogatory term used to refer to a more decadent side of Laika.

subgenres.name: Tallava
subgenres.desc: Mixture of Romani, Greek, Turkish, Albanian, and Slavic music, which incorporates Dance-Pop elements, and is very popular in Albania and Kosovo.

subgenres.name: Turbo-Folk
subgenres.desc: Originated in Serbia during the 1980s, fusing traditional Western Balkan Folk Music with elements of contemporary popular music.

subgenres.name: Baroque Pop
subgenres.desc: Incorporates elements of Western Classical Music, commonly featuring harpsichord or strings as well as the rhythmic flow and counterpoint of Baroque Music.

subgenres.name: Bitpop
subgenres.desc: Fuses Bit Music with additional synths, beats, guitars and modern production values, emphasizing highly catchy melodies and relatively fast tempos.

subgenres.name: Blue-Eyed Soul
subgenres.desc: Usually refers to a Pop or Pop Rock song that contains strong Gospel-like elements, primarily popularized by white American and British singers in the 1960s through the 1980s.

subgenres.name: Boy Band
subgenres.desc: Male vocal groups often put together by talent managers or record producers.

subgenres.name: Brega calypso
subgenres.desc: Romantic vocals and lyrics, bubbly and sensual melodies and rhythms, horn sections and lush Caribbean-like guitar riffs over fast tempos.

subgenres.name: Brill Building
subgenres.desc: Elaborate, polished, and typically melodramatic composition and arrangement associated with the songwriting teams at the Brill office building during the late 1950s and early 1960s.

subgenres.name: Bubblegum
subgenres.desc: Upbeat, catchy, simple, and targeted at children and young teens; especially popular in the 1960s and 1970s.

subgenres.name: Cambodian Pop
subgenres.desc: Popular music produced in Cambodia or by Khmer people.

subgenres.name: Rom kbach
subgenres.desc: Cambodian pop with a slow melody that is similar to Luk thung.

subgenres.name: Canción melódica
subgenres.desc: Sentimental vocal music sung in Spanish with a focus on the chorus, originally developed in the first half of the 20th century from a variety of traditional Hispanic genres.

subgenres.name: Bolero-Beat
subgenres.desc: Latin American style stemming from both Canción melódica and the British Beat.

subgenres.name: Música cebolla
subgenres.desc: Chilean offshoot of Canción melódica that expresses a much more melancholic or nostalgic side.

subgenres.name: City Pop
subgenres.desc: Wave of Japanese Pop intended to reflect urban life during the period of the country's booming economy in the 1970s and 1980s, featuring a contemporary Western sound and lush arrangements.

subgenres.name: Neo-City Pop
subgenres.desc: 2010s style blending emerging genres like Acid Jazz and Neo-Soul with the Western-inspired Japanese Pop styles of the 1970s and 1980s.

subgenres.name: Classical Crossover
subgenres.desc: Takes specific Western Classical Music conventions and applies them into a straightfoward Pop context for mainstream appeal.

subgenres.name: Country Pop
subgenres.desc: Combination of Country with Pop to appeal to a larger audience.

subgenres.name: Boyfriend Country
subgenres.desc: Soft, sentimental, and acoustic-leaning style featuring romantic lyrics, slick Contemporary R&B stylings, and light percussion.

subgenres.name: Bro-Country
subgenres.desc: 21st century style with an often party-oriented sound and lyrical content, taking strong influence from Hard Rock, Hip Hop and Pop.

subgenres.name: Countrypolitan
subgenres.desc: Emphasizes Pop-oriented orchestration and songwriting while reducing the role of Country instrumentation and rhythms; often featuring lush string arrangements and group backing vocals.

subgenres.name: Urban Cowboy
subgenres.desc: Melds Country and 1970s L.A. soft Pop, sometimes leaning towards Disco.

subgenres.name: Dance-Pop
subgenres.desc: Simple, catchy melodies and throbbing beats inspired initially by Disco and later various House styles.

subgenres.name: Bubblegum Dance
subgenres.desc: Playful, childlike style with a Bubblegum-like atmosphere that often incorporates high-pitched, light-hearted, and usually female-fronted vocals.

subgenres.name: Disco polo
subgenres.desc: Polish Dance-Pop, originally established from contemporary wedding / feast songs and Italo-Disco.

subgenres.name: Freestyle
subgenres.desc: Electro-influenced; developed in Latino communities in New York and Miami in the 1980s, especially dominated by Latin Freestyle and its Latin influences.

subgenres.name: Latin Freestyle
subgenres.desc: Displays a heavy influence of Hispanic American Music alongside the Disco, Hip Hop, and Electro influences of Freestyle.

subgenres.name: Funk melody
subgenres.desc: Light and melodic take on Funk brasileiro, developed alongside Funk carioca.

subgenres.name: Romanian Popcorn
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the second half of the 2000s in Romania, often featuring brass melodies and "staccato" pluck grooves.

subgenres.name: Tecnorumba
subgenres.desc: Blend of the themes and singing style of Rumba flamenca with the most commercial forms of House, Techno, and Makina.

subgenres.name: Township Bubblegum
subgenres.desc: Synth-heavy Dance-Pop style popular in the South African townships in the 1980s and early 1990s.

subgenres.name: Dangdut
subgenres.desc: Indonesian popular music distinguished by a rhythmic blend of Indian, Arabic, Western, Malay, Sundanese, and Javanese influences within Indonesian Music, characterized by a unique rhythmic pattern from kendang.

subgenres.name: Dangdut koplo
subgenres.desc: Development of Dangdut which originated in East Java in the 1990s, featuring a faster tempo and influences from international styles like Pop, Rock, and Reggae.

subgenres.name: Dansbandsmusik
subgenres.desc: Nordic Pop style originating from 1960s Pop Rock, incorporating Swing, Schlager, Nordic Old Time Dance Music and Country influences.

subgenres.name: Dansktop
subgenres.desc: Danish equivalent to Dansbandsmusik with Schlager and Country influences and Contemporary Folk and Pop elements.

subgenres.name: Electro Hop
subgenres.desc: Emerged in the mid 2000s featuring upbeat rap verses and catchy hooks over four-on-the-floor Electropop and  Electro House-inspired production.

subgenres.name: Electropop
subgenres.desc: Dense, layered, and compressed production, usually coupled with a distinct fuzzy and "warm" low-frequency synthesizer style.

subgenres.name: Europop
subgenres.desc: Emerged throughout mainland Europe in the early 1970s, referring to slick, highly commercial Pop songs that emphasize sugary melodies and light, bouncy instrumentation.

subgenres.name: Flamenco Pop
subgenres.desc: Incorporates Flamenco sub-styles into a more commercial Pop form; particularly through the vocal style and rhythms.

subgenres.name: Folk Pop
subgenres.desc: Blends Contemporary Folk with a Pop sensibility, most popular in the late 1960s and early 1970s and featuring influence from the contemporary Folk Rock style.

subgenres.name: Stomp and Holler
subgenres.desc: Highlights driving "stomping" rhythms and shouted group vocal harmonies, often drawing influences from Pop Rock, Indie Folk, and other genres, while maintaining a characteristically mellow and commercial sound.

subgenres.name: French Pop
subgenres.desc: Pop originating from France.

subgenres.name: Girl Group
subgenres.desc: Combines elements of Rhythm & Blues, Rock & Roll, and Traditional Pop; typically performed by trios or quartets of female vocalists.

subgenres.name: Hmong Pop
subgenres.desc: Popular music of the Hmong ethnicity, with roots in the Hmong Folk Music and influenced by Western and East Asian forms of Pop music.

subgenres.name: Hyperpop
subgenres.desc: Developed and took inspiration from Bubblegum Bass and popular 2000s-2010s Electropop, characterized by eclectic, unconventional, mechanical-sounding and dense production; and by manipulated, usually auto-tuned vocals.

subgenres.name: Indian Pop
subgenres.desc: Commonly based out of India, Pakistan and Bangladesh and almost always sung in Hindi, Urdu or Bengali, implements South Asian Music in context of American and European Pop and Rock music.

subgenres.name: Bhojpuri Pop
subgenres.desc: Modernized pop-folk variant of Bhojpuri Folk Music.

subgenres.name: Indie Pop
